scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Pursere Kattuna is a religious and traditional folk dance form of Tulunadu, performed mainly in the villages of Belthangady taluk in the Dakshina Kannada district of Karnataka, India, by Tulu-speaking people from various castes.
The style shows influence from the Natha Pantha spiritual tradition.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Held during the full moon in the Suggi month, the ritual blesses homes with healing, prosperity, and protection.
It combines ritual healing, traditional belief, humor, performance art, and community theatre, preserving oral narratives and mythic storytelling.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance takes place from late evening until the early hours of the morning during the full moon in the month of Suggi.
Dancers visit homes of different social strata, engaging in acting, singing, dancing, symbolic storytelling, and mythological mimicry while interacting with each other and the public.
on_screen: Formation: Dancers visit the homes of people belonging to different social strata across villages of Belthangady taluk.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The musical accompaniment is provided by instruments including the Tase, Dolu, Nadaswara, and Shruti, which guide the rhythm of the dance, mythic dialogues, and singing sequences throughout the night.
Listen for the Tase, Dolu, Nadaswara, Shruti.
Guided by the percussive strike of Tase and Dolu drums alongside the resonant tones of Nadaswara and Shruti, the music drives nocturnal singing sequences and mythic dialogues throughout the night.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes represent diverse roles such as Brahmins, priests, mendicants, ascetics, fortune tellers, Koti Chennaya, wild animals (bears, tigers, lions, monkeys), scholars, thieves, ghosts, spiritual entities, a Christian male, a Muslim female, and farcical characters.
A similar performance in Sullia uses the Siddavesha costume style featuring Sanyasi, Bhatru, and Dasayye.
